set.tagline: A pig farmer, a sword, and a world that never learned to take its hero seriously.
set.description: Robinson Technologies' free, expanded edition of the 1997 action RPG brings smoother graphics, quick saves, gamepad support and a built-in browser for hundreds of fan-made DMOD adventures.

qualityBar.verdict: Dink's jokes get you through the door; the fan-made adventures keep finding new rooms behind it.

set.longDescription:
Dink Smallwood begins with a pig farmer who would be much happier if the world stopped asking him to be a hero. Seth Robinson's original 1997 action RPG is openly silly, but it has a proper adventure under the jokes: explore, talk to people, learn to fight, and follow a story that keeps finding excuses to make Dink uncomfortable. The odd tone is part of its identity. It is difficult to mistake this for a carefully solemn fantasy epic, and that is precisely why it still feels distinct.

Dink Smallwood HD is the newer Robinson Technologies build rather than an unrelated fan remake. The HD engine adds smooth scrolling and higher-resolution rendering, quick save and load, touchscreen input, and support for both XInput and DirectInput controllers. Those are concrete improvements to a game whose original presentation can feel as old as its jokes. You can play the main adventure on its own and understand why people stayed with it.

The much longer story is the DMOD scene. DMODs are player-made Dink adventures, not cosmetic packs. The HD edition includes a browser that can download and install hundreds of them. That makes the base campaign a starting point for a library of new maps and stories built by a community that has been making things for this game for years. A mod browser inside the game means the path from finishing the main story to trying someone's strange new quest is unusually short. It also explains why a 1997 RPG keeps getting fresh conversations.

GOG lists Dink Smallwood HD as a free, DRM-free Windows game; the developer's own RTDink repository links a signed Windows installer, a notarized universal Mac DMG for macOS 11 or newer, and a Linux Flatpak. We checked those download endpoints. The older Draft page called it a commercial purchase, warned about unsigned open-source installers, and guessed at its size. Those claims were wrong. The game has native controller input, but PlayBound has not yet play-tested a specific pad layout, so the engine's support is more certain than any custom Controls profile. It is a single-player game; the DMOD browser does not turn it into an online party or dedicated-server title.

We like Dink because its creators made it easy to keep playing and easy for other people to add to. Start with the original tale, laugh at a joke that has no business surviving this long, then look at what another player built out of the same tools. The game belongs as much to that continuing chain of adventures as it does to its first campaign.
set.whyWePickedIt: Dink Smallwood HD gives a genuinely free, complete RPG a friendly modern entry point. Native gamepad support helps, but the built-in DMOD browser is the larger reason: it lets one small 1997 adventure open into years of community-made quests.
set.thatOneThing: Dink can finish saving the world and immediately open an in-game browser to see what fresh disaster another player wrote for him.

installSteps.text: Download the signed DinkSmallwoodHDInstaller.exe from Robinson Technologies, or add the free GOG Windows release to your library and use GOG's offline installer. Run the installer and launch Dink Smallwood HD.
Download the developer's DinkSmallwoodHD.dmg, open it, and copy the notarized universal app into Applications. The developer lists macOS 11 or newer.
Download the developer's x86_64 Flatpak and install it with Flatpak, then launch com.rtsoft.DinkSmallwoodHD. ARM users should use the developer's aarch64 Flatpak instead.
After the main campaign starts, open the HD edition's DMOD browser to browse player-made adventures. No multiplayer server or proprietary base-game data is required.

firstPlaySteps.text: Start the main Dink Smallwood story, choose keyboard or a gamepad in the game's options, and try quick save before opening a DMOD.

faq.a: Yes. GOG lists the Windows release as a free game, and Robinson Technologies publishes free Windows, Mac and Linux downloads.
The HD edition is an enhanced build of the original 1997 RPG, with improved rendering, quick saves, controller and touch support, and a built-in DMOD browser.

faq.q: Can I play with a controller?
faq.a: Yes. The developer and GOG both document native DirectInput and XInput controller support. PlayBound has not yet verified a custom controller profile for every pad.
No multiplayer mode is documented for this HD edition. DMODs are additional single-player adventures, not online servers.

faq.q: How do Mac and Linux installs work?
faq.a: The developer provides a universal macOS DMG for macOS 11+ and x86_64/aarch64 Flatpaks for Linux. PlayBound has not verified automated Flatpak installation.

bestFor: Players who enjoy oddball fantasy RPGs with a sense of humor
Anyone who likes a main campaign followed by a deep library of community adventures
notFor: Friends seeking co-op or online multiplayer
Players who want a serious, straight-faced fantasy story
